YC partner Harshita Arora is coming to Purdue to give an off-the-record talk about startups.

She'll share what YC has learned from funding companies like Stripe, Twitch, Reddit, and Scale AI, which were all started by college drop-outs or new grads.

You don't need to be working on a startup to attend. In fact, Harshita is especially interested in talking to students studying technical subjects like CS, math and engineering who may not have thought much about doing a startup yet.

If you are already working on a startup and would like to do a 1-1 coffee chat with Harshita to talk about it, she'd love to meet you. There's a separate signup for that here.

It’d be stupid not to apply for $100K

Hi everyone,

The 38th Burton D. Morgan Venture Concept Competition is the biggest competition happening this semester, with a $100,000 prize pool.

I genuinely think it’d be stupid not to participate if you’re interested in entrepreneurship, especially if you’re already working on a startup. Yes, you can apply with the startup you’re already building.

All you need to do today is put one idea down in the concept submission form: https://www.buildpurdue.org/go/burton-morgan-competition-2026-instagram-1. It doesn’t need to be fully figured out, and you could of thought of it this morning or asked ChatGPT for one. Over 10 weeks, you’ll develop and test it through workshops, customer discovery, and feedback, then present at the final event on December 11. You can pivot, tweak, or completely change your idea ANYTIME (like a real startup).

You just have to apply by TONGHT: Sunday, September 27, at 11:59 p.m. If you don’t apply today, you won’t have the chance to participate.

🏆 Competition details: https://www.buildpurdue.org/go/burton-morgan-competition-2026-instagram-2
🚀 Apply here: https://www.buildpurdue.org/go/burton-morgan-competition-2026-instagram-1

- Elliot
